Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Financial Group third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Financial Group's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Credit Officer; David Kim, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Ellis, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Financial Group delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on accelerating revenue growth, improving profitability, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our performance. We achieved robust deposit growth of 4.2% quarter-over-quarter, with a favorable mix shift supporting our funding strategy. Net interest income rose to $2.52 billion, up 2% sequentially, with guidance pointing to further expansion in Q4. Loan growth was strong at 7.2% year-over-year across segments, driven by commercial and consumer momentum. Credit quality improved markedly, with our NPL ratio at 0.82%. We're advancing our capital return plans, including a 10% dividend increase and ongoing share repurchases. Fee income hit $5.2 billion, up 12%, led by wealth management, investment banking, and cards. Finally, non-interest income showed resilience at $2.8 billion, benefiting from market tailwinds in trading and capital markets despite volatility.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. UniBank Financial Group reported net income of $1.75 billion for the third quarter, or $1.48 per diluted share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 2% quarter-over-quarter to $2.52 billion, driven by asset repricing in our commercial portfolios and the stability of our low-cost deposit base. Non-interest income was up 5% sequentially to $2.8 billion, reflecting strong performance in trading revenues and investment banking fees.

Turning first to our deposit franchise, which remains a cornerstone of our funding strategy. In this high-rate environment with the Fed funds rate at 5.25% to 5.50%, deposit competition has intensified from traditional peers like JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America, as well as digital players such as Ally Financial and Marcus by Goldman Sachs offering APYs above 4.5% on high-yield savings. Despite this pressure, we delivered solid deposit growth in Q3, highlighting the power of our relationship-driven model and targeted initiatives.

Total deposits reached $258.7 billion at quarter-end, up 4.2% quarter-over-quarter and 11.8% year-over-year—outpacing the industry average of 2-3% QoQ per the latest FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile. Excluding brokered CDs used sparingly for liquidity, core customer deposits grew 5.1% QoQ to $242.4 billion. This kept our loan-to-deposit ratio at a stable 82.6%, down 150 basis points from Q2, giving us plenty of room for lending while maintaining a fortress balance sheet.

Regionally, our Southeast markets saw strong 7.2% QoQ growth from market share gains in Florida and Texas small business areas, where we've expanded UniBiz payroll deposit programs with local employers. Northeast urban centers grew more modestly at 2.8% QoQ due to some outflows to money market funds yielding 5.2%, but we're addressing this head-on. Western regions advanced 3.9%, supported by treasury management partnerships with California tech firms.

Our deposit mix evolved positively, balancing cost control with competitiveness. Transactional deposits, including non-interest-bearing DDA and NOW accounts, make up 44% or $113.8 billion, up 3.1% QoQ. Year-to-date, they've risen 9.5%, powered by cross-selling treasury services like ACH sweeps and zero-balance accounts to our commercial clients, with non-interest-bearing at 28% of the total thanks to 95%+ retention among relationship households.

Savings deposits, at 37% or $95.7 billion, grew fastest at 6.8% QoQ as customers sought yield, with our UniSavings Plus product—tiered up to 4.35% APY for balances over $50,000—bringing in $4.2 billion in net new funds. This segment yields 2.85% on average, up 15 basis points but still 220 basis points below our blended cost of funds at 5.05%.

Time deposits, 19% or $49.2 billion, increased 2.9% QoQ, mainly short-term brokered CDs through IntraFi Network for duration management. Retail CDs, 12% of this, saw modest growth via selective 4.75% 12-month specials for high-net-worth clients, steering clear of rate wars.

The mix shifted 100 basis points toward savings from transactional, lifting deposit beta to 45%—aligned with peers like Wells Fargo—but core stability drove 12 basis point NIM expansion to 3.62%.

Key trends include rate sensitivity with $1.2 billion in transactional outflows to MMFs as 3-month Treasuries hit 5.35%, though tapering with CPI at 3.2%; a digital shift where mobile inflows surged 28% YoY via our UniBank app, countering 1-2% fintech share loss in younger demographics; and commercial stickiness with CRE and C&I deposits up 8.4% offsetting consumer swings, aided by recession-driven precautionary balances up 12% YoY average.

To keep this going, our Core+Growth strategy includes launching UniYield Ladder in Q4—a CD ladder tool with our robo-advisor—for $3-5 billion inflows at 4.5% blended APY; $150 million in 2023 CapEx for API open banking with Plaid for P2P and yield alerts; an AI retention engine cutting churn 22% via personalized nudges; expanding UniPremier to 500,000 households for 15% cross-sell; Relationship Manager 2.0 lifting transactional per client 18%; and Southeast branch growth plus Northeast brokered reciprocals.

We guide 4-6% QoQ core deposit growth in Q4, costs stabilizing with 45-50 bps beta compression, NIM to 3.70%+ in 2024, supporting 8-10% loan growth with HQLA at 125%.

Now, on net interest income and Q4 guidance. NII of $2.52 billion beat our prior midpoint by $25 million, up 7% YoY and 2% QoQ, with FTE NIM at 3.48%, third straight quarter of 12 bps expansion—better than Wells Fargo and U.S. Bancorp's 3.20-3.30%.

Assets grew 4% YoY to $285 billion, with 6% C&I expansion in tech services and healthcare at 5.85% yields. Consumer loans up 2% via AI scoring reducing delinquencies to 2.1%. CRE flat at $42 billion, office limited to 8%.

Deposits up 5% YoY to $240 billion, core transactional at 68%, beta at 32% vs. peers' 40%. Digital added 150,000 non-interest accounts. Costs at 1.92%, wholesale low at 8%, LCR 145%. Southeast up 8%, Midwest C&I 7%, Europe $120 million NII.

For Q4, NII $2.58-2.68 billion, NIM 3.50-3.55%, assuming two 25 bps Fed cuts to 4.50%. EPS $1.52-1.62, PPNR $3.4-3.5 billion, non-interest $1.1 billion from ECM and payments. Expenses $2.2 billion, 58% efficiency via $50 million GenAI savings. Provisions $350-400 million.

We're optimizing via ALM swaps at 5.2% on $10 billion securities, treasury services at 25% commercial revenue, CET1 11.8%, $1.2 billion buybacks, 3% dividend hike.

Shifting to loan growth by segment, average loans up 7.2% YoY to $285 billion—10th straight quarter beating FDIC's 4.8% industry. Commercial at 52% or $148 billion grew 11.5% YoY, 2.8% sequential: C&I +13.2% on manufacturing/tech capex, middle-market drawdowns +15%; CRE +9.8% to $62 billion, multifamily/industrial +12-14%, office flat, modified LTV 62%. Tech platform with Salesforce/nCino up closure 22%, Southeast 40% inflows, ABL +18%, syndications. Expect 10-12% FY25.

Consumer 28% or $80 billion +6.8% YoY: auto +9.5% to $42 billion, FICO 740, indirect 65%; personal +7.2% via Rocket Loans app; cards +4.1% to $18 billion, rewards +15%. Midwest 35%, BNPL $1.2 billion, NIM 5.8%, guide 6-8%.

Mortgage 20% or $57 billion +2.4% YoY: originations $4.8 billion +18% QoQ at 6.5% rates, purchase 85%; jumbo HFI +4.2%, HELOC +11% to $12 billion at 80% LTV. Sun Belt 50%, Blend platform +30% conversion, non-QM. Delinquency 0.9%, 3-5% '25 growth.

Balanced mix yields 5.6% up 45 bps, CET1 11.2%, organic funded by 8.2% deposits.

On credit quality, NPL ratio at 0.82% down 18 bps QoQ/35 bps YoY—below 1% target, better than JPM's 0.95%/Wells' 1.05%. Delinquencies 1.95% down 25 bps QoQ/60 bps YoY. Charge-offs 42 bps or $185 million down from 55/68 bps, core 38 bps. Provisions $320 million, ACL 1.45% loans/175% NPLs.

Consumer strong: cards NPL 2.1% from 2.6%, auto 1.2% delinq vs 1.8%, mortgage 0.9%. C&I 0.65%, CRE office 1.4% with $450 million migrations, 8% exposure LTV 65%, SMB 0.9%. Southeast 0.55%, Midwest 2.4% energy workouts $120 million, Europe 1.1%, Asia 0.7%.

Higher rates pressure but boost margins; consumer net worth $156T; EWS ML flagged 15% fewer risks. GenAI monitoring cut false positives 22%, deferrals kept 65% current, CRE stress/syndications $2 billion. NPLs low-80s bps, charge-offs 40 bps base, excess ACL $1.2 billion downside.

Capital returns: Board approved 10% quarterly dividend hike to $0.53/share, 17th annual increase, TTM $2.12, 3.2% yield, 42% payout vs 35-50% target. Organic capital $8.2 billion YTD, NII +12% beta 28%, ROTCE 13.8%, DFAST +200 bps over 11.5%.

Q3 buybacks $1.1 billion/15 million shares at $42.50, YTD $3.2 billion/2.5% shares, 3% EPS accretion. 2024 target $7-8 billion 60/40 split, $4 billion new auth to $5.5 billion. Opportunistic >$45 EPS/11.5% CET1.

U.S. deposits $25 billion YTD 95% retention/UniMobile 18 million users; EMEA CET1 13.2% €500 million Q4; APAC Tencent fees +28%. 2025 $1.2-1.4 EPS, 58% efficiency, NII $28-29 billion. $22 billion returned 3 years.

Fee income $5.2 billion +12% YoY, 28% revenues, core +10% ex $150 million gain. Wealth mgmt $2.34 billion +15%, 45% fees: NNM $28 billion, AUM $1.25T +11%, 75 bps, equities rally S&P +8%, alts +18%, ESG +25% UniGreen, Americas +16%, APAC +22%, AI UniWealth +15% cross-sell, 85% recurring '25.

IB $1.56 billion +8%, 30%: M&A $850 million +12% tech/healthcare, ECM/DCM $710 million +5-10%, #4 M&A/#6 ECM, U.S. 55% +10%, APAC +15%, Quantum DealFlow +20% bids, blockchain syndication. Mid-teens Q4.

Cards $1.30 billion +18%, 25%: interchange $780 million +20% Visa/MC premium +30%, annual/late $350 +12%, other $170 +22%, U.S. 70% +16%, APAC +35%, GenAI fraud -40% chargebacks, tokenization, $6 billion run-rate '24 65% margins.

Non-interest income $2.8 billion +12% YoY/5% QoQ, 28% mix. IB $850 million +18%: ECM $120 million NexGen IPO, HY $25 billion 450 bps spreads, M&A -5% QoQ reg scrutiny, market share 7.2% Americas, APAC +25%, Helix AI +15% wins.

Trading $1.1 billion +22%: FICC $650 +28% MOVE 135, FX +35% EM, equities $450 +14% PB $450 billion +19%, algo 65% +200 bps, Americas 60%, APAC +30%. $250 million quantum/low-latency.

AWM $620 million +9%: AUM $1.7T +14%, NNM $45 billion, ETFs $12 billion, perf $80 million PE 10.5x, U.S. HNW +12%, EMEA UCITS €5 billion, APAC $8 billion, open arch 40% 96% retention.

Service/cards $330 +6%: interchange $180 +10% Shopify/Stripe $120 billion, treasury $800 billion +20%, digital +25%.

Markets added $110 million via rates/VIX/equities; risks S&P drawdown/Basel. $400 million GenAI/blockchain, APAC JVs, alts 25%.

Our capital ratios remain strong at CET1 11.8%, positioning us well for growth.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, commercial real estate exposures particularly in office sectors, and cybersecurity threats in our digital channels. We are taking proactive steps like enhanced stress testing incorporating BlackRock forecasts, AI-driven early warning systems, and syndication of higher-risk assets to mitigate these and maintain our strong risk profile.

Lisa Patel:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loans at 0.82% and delinquencies at 1.95%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio across commercial, consumer, and mortgage segments and remain confident in navigating the current environment. Specifically, the performance of our commercial real estate portfolio has been resilient with conservative LTVs and limited office exposure.

David Kim:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on digital transformation, including the rollout of GenAI for portfolio monitoring, fraud detection, and personalized wealth advice, alongside platforms like UniWealth Advisor, Quantum DealFlow, and integrations with Plaid, Salesforce, nCino, and Blend. These have driven customer adoption surges, like 2.5 million Rocket Loans users and 18 million UniMobile actives, plus efficiency gains reducing churn 22%, approval times to 60 seconds, and false positives 22%.

Robert Ellis:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency. Key initiatives include GenAI back-office reconciliation and productivity savings targeting $200 million annualized by mid-2025, alongside open banking APIs and merchant ecosystem expansions, contributing to improved productivity, cost savings, and a 58% efficiency ratio.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Sullivan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Sullivan:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into deposit growth and mix trends and strategies?

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, Mike. As Sarah detailed, our 4.2% QoQ growth to $258.7 billion, with core up 5.1%, reflects our relationship focus amid competition. Transactional at 44%, savings 37% via UniSavings Plus, time 19%. Strategies like UniYield Ladder, AI retention, UniPremier, and Southeast expansion guide us to 4-6% Q4 growth, stabilizing costs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee:
What are your plans for NII and earnings guidance for the next quarter?

Sarah Thompson:
Hi Jennifer. Q4 NII $2.58-2.68 billion, NIM 3.50-3.55% on two Fed cuts, deposit beta 35%, loan growth. Adjusted EPS $1.52-1.62, PPNR $3.4-3.5 billion, non-interest $1.1 billion, expenses $2.2 billion. Conservative on outflows or CRE.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
How are you managing credit quality amid economic uncertainty?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, David. Our NPLs at 0.82%, charge-offs 42 bps reflect proactive management. EWS ML, GenAI PD/LGD, workouts, CRE syndications keep us covered 1.25x criticized, excess ACL for downside.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Can you discuss the performance of loan growth by segment?

Lisa Patel:
Sure, Emily. Overall 7.2% YoY to $285 billion. Commercial +11.5% C&I 13.2%, CRE 9.8%; consumer +6.8% auto 9.5%; mortgage +2.4% HELOC 11%. Disciplined underwriting, regional strength, tech platforms driving this.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
